summary: Today’s PaymentsDive recap: 8 new stories, with focus on fraud/security, regulation.

articles.title: Visa adapts to tech innovations
articles.description: The card network’s fiscal 2026 results show it’s reaching beyond legacy payments paths to incorporate new technologies, offer new services and extend its global reach with more partners.

articles.title: Liability looms over AI shopping
articles.description: Some banks and other payment players lament how agentic commerce has steamrolled ahead without “rules of the road” for liability issues.

articles.title: Venmo results lift PayPal
articles.description: The digital payments processor is benefiting from its peer-to-peer payment tool business after cutting 2,000 employee jobs.

articles.title: USDA proposes adding chip and tap-to-pay tech to EBT cards
articles.description: The National Grocers Association said the payment technologies, which are currently available in nearly a dozen states, can help reduce SNAP fraud.

articles.title: Fed loses debit card cap appeal
articles.description: The Federal Reserve’s debit card interchange rule doesn’t follow the intent of Congress in setting a limit for swipe fees, an appellate court ruled Monday.

articles.title: Euronet, Fireblocks pursue stablecoin cards
articles.description: The companies are extending their partnership to provide financial firms with the infrastructure needed to issue stablecoin-funded cards.

articles.title: Why checks still matter
articles.description: At a major industry conference this month, the paper instrument kept cropping up in discussions, even with an agenda focused on digital modernization.

articles.title: The B2B payment stack wasn’t built for how businesses pay now
articles.description: The B2B payment decision used to be binary. Legacy infrastructure still is.
